message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to launch a **Compute‑Engine** VM that has a high‑performance NVIDIA GPU attached – one via the `gcloud` CLI and another via the raw REST API (`instances.insert`).  
Because Google Cloud Platform (GCP) doesn’t yet offer the *RTX A6000* card (it only supports Tesla cards such as V100, A100, T4, etc.), the examples use the closest equivalent—an **NVIDIA Tesla A100** (or V100 if you prefer something cheaper).  

---

### 1️⃣ Create the instance with the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables -------------------------------------------------------------
INSTANCE_NAME="my-radeon-instance"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick your preferred zone
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-highmem-16" # adjust CPU/RAM per your workload
GPU_COUNT=1                   # how many GPUs you want
GPU_MODEL="nvidia-a100"       # change to v100/t4/k80/etc if you wish
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
    --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional init script
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure=true \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --labels=gcp-demo=yes \
    --accelerators=count=${GPU_COUNT},type=${GPU_MODEL}
```

#### What each flag means

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | Number of CPUs & RAM |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root volume |
| `--image-*` | Base OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS) |
| `--accelerators` | Attach GPU(s); replace `${GPU_MODEL}` with `nvidia-k80`, `v100`, `t4`, or `a100`. |

> ⚠️ **Important:** Replace `"${GPU_MODEL}"` with a GPU type actually available in your region. Use `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zones $ZONE` to see what’s offered.

---

### 2️⃣ Same thing via the REST API (`instances.insert`)

If you’re calling the API programmatically (e.g., from Terraform, Pulumi, or custom code), here’s a minimal JSON payload you’d POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances`.

```json
{
  "kind": "compute#regionInstance",
  "name": "my-radeon-instance",
  "description": "VM with NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.",
  "machineType": "projects/myproject/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-highmem-16",

  "disks": [
    {
      "deviceName": "bootdisk",
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50
      }
    }
  ],

  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type":"ONE_TO_ONE_NAT","name":"External NAT"}]
    }
  ],

  "serviceAccounts": [{
    "email": "default",
    "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  }],

  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/myproject/zones/us-central1-b/types/nvidia-a100"
    }
  ]
}
```

Replace:
- `myproject` → Your actual project ID.
- `us-central1-b` → Desired zone.
- `nvidia-a100` → Any other GPU type you have permission to attach.

Send this payload with OAuth 2.0 authentication (Bearer token) to the endpoint above. You can also add additional fields such as metadata scripts, labels, firewall rules, etc., depending on your requirements.

---

### Quick sanity check

Before launching anything, confirm the GPU availability in your target zone:

```bash
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zones us-central1-b
```

Look for entries like `nvidia-a100`, `nvidia-v100`, `nvidia-t4`, etc. If “RTX A6000” appears, great! Otherwise stick with the listed options.

---

Feel free to tweak machine types, disk sizes, network settings, or even swap out the base image (for example, `debian-cloud/debian-10`) according to your workflow. Happy computing!
